landmarks.name: Vaduz Castle
landmarks.writeup: The official residence of the Prince of Liechtenstein, perched on a hill overlooking the capital Vaduz.

wiki.extract: Vaduz Castle is the palace and official residence of the Prince of Liechtenstein. The castle gave its name to the town of Vaduz, the capital of Liechtenstein, which it overlooks from an adjacent hilltop.

landmarks.name: Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein
landmarks.writeup: A modern art museum in Vaduz featuring contemporary and modern art collections.

wiki.extract: Liechtenstein, officially the Principality of Liechtenstein, is a doubly landlocked country in the Central European Alps. A microstate, It is located between Austria to the east and north-east and Switzerland to the north-west, west and south.

landmarks.name: Gutenberg Castle
landmarks.writeup: A well-preserved medieval castle located in the town of Balzers.

wiki.extract: Gutenberg Castle is an intact castle in the municipality of Balzers, Liechtenstein, the southern-most municipality in the country. Gutenberg is one of the five castles of the principality and one of two that have survived intact until the present day.

cultural_events.name: Vaduz Film Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual event showcasing international and local films, promoting cultural exchange.

wiki.extract: Dracula, Prisoner of Frankenstein is a 1972 horror film directed by Jesús Franco and starring Dennis Price, Howard Vernon, Alberto Dalbés, Carmen Yazalde and Luis Barboo.

cultural_events.name: National Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on August 15th with speeches, fireworks, and traditional festivities.

wiki.extract: A national day is a day on which celebrations mark the statehood or nationhood of a state or its people. It may be the date of independence, of becoming a republic, of becoming a federation, or a significant date for a patron saint, a ruler or a date in that country's particular history.

food_writeup: Liechtenstein cuisine is influenced by Swiss and Austrian traditions, featuring dishes like Käsknöpfle (cheese noodles), Ribel (cornmeal dish), and various hearty meat and potato meals.
brief_history: Liechtenstein was established as a principality in 1719 within the Holy Roman Empire. It remained neutral during both World Wars and developed into a prosperous financial center in the 20th century.

important_people.name: Franz Joseph II
important_people.description: Former Prince who modernized the country
